h1: URL to Video: Turn a Product Link into a Video Ad
lead: Your product page already has a good photo and a name, but turning that listing into an ad clip usually means starting a shoot from scratch. Paste the link into URL to Video and build the clip from the exact variant you sell, without uploading files or shipping samples.

benefits_h2: Why start a video ad from a product link?

benefits.d: The link supplies the product photo and name, so you don't have to export and re-upload assets before making the ad.

benefits.t: Starts from the variant you sell
benefits.d: Review the captured image and name first, so the clip shows the same color and version listed on the page.
Write the action or spoken line and choose the final pose, keeping every claim tied to facts you control.
If the page blocks access or picks the wrong image, replace it with your own upload without leaving the flow.

steps_h2: How to make a video ad from a product link in 3 simple steps
steps_lead: Three steps turn a public product page link into a ready-to-post clip — no shoot, no sample shipment.

steps.d: Paste a public product page that loads without sign-in. The tool reads its main image and name when the page allows access.
Check the image, name, color and variant, and replace the photo if needed. Then choose the one selling point to show.
Describe one action or spoken line, choose the length and final pose, then download. Add your offer and price in your editor.

faq.a: A public product page can still block access or require a login. If it does, upload the product photo instead. Use a page that loads without a sign-in and shows the variant you want.

faq.q: What do you take from the page?
faq.a: Only the main product photo and the product name. Prices, reviews and other text on the page are not used. The captured image may differ from the gallery image, so compare it manually.

faq.q: Can I use a link to someone else's product?
faq.a: Only use links to products you own or are allowed to advertise, and only photos you have the rights to use. Confirm that your rights cover the product image, name and advertising use.

faq.q: Can I change the photo you picked?
faq.a: Yes. If the photo isn't the best one, replace it with your own upload before you generate. Check the replacement photo before writing the action prompt.

faq.q: What does a product URL provide?
faq.a: It reads public page metadata and available product imagery from the URL, then uses that reference for the clip. Use a stable product photo when the page offers several gallery variants.

faq.q: What if the page cannot be read?
faq.a: Use a direct product photo in the upload flow when the page blocks access or exposes no usable image. A direct upload avoids a blocked page and gives you more control over the starting frame.

faq.q: Does the link include prices or reviews?
faq.a: No. The tool uses the available product image and product name as the visual reference. Add your own price, review wording and offer in the editor after generation so every public claim is current. Recheck wording after generation because product facts can change.

faq.q: Can I choose a different variant after capture?
faq.a: Yes. Replace the captured image with a clear upload when the page selected the wrong color, size or angle. Check the replacement against the item you ship before you describe the motion. Save the chosen variant before you describe motion so color and scale stay consistent.

faq.q: Do I need a product page to make the video?
faq.a: No. A public link is the fastest starting point, but if the page blocks access or has no usable image, upload a product photo and describe the scene the same way. Both routes end with the same kind of clip built around your product.

faq.q: Can I use the video as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download is watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, so you can run it on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook or another ad channel. Put prices and offers in your ad tool, since the page text and reviews are not copied into the clip.

overview.h2: Start with the product page you already have
overview.p: A public product page provides the starting photo and name. Share your video idea in one sentence, such as opening a lid or lifting a bag, to turn the listing into a short scene.

examples.lead: See how creators can demonstrate products with a try-on, an unboxing, a routine or a clear before-and-after. Each format turns the page reference into one visible action that can carry a specific hook in a paid placement.

picker.title: Choose a product ad format
picker.lead: Choose a scene that shows a product in use, on camera or in a creator-led ad. Match the action to the shopper question, then keep one product, one setting and one final pose in the prompt.

Natural creator-review framing, chest-up vertical shot. Sound: spoken line and quiet room tone; no music.

uses.d: Start with a public product page that includes a clear product image and name. Confirm the URL is public and points to the exact item or variant you want to advertise. Record the captured page state before you request another variant.

The product image and name become the starting reference for the video request. Review both before generation so the action does not begin with a mismatched color, size or product family. Keep one final pose so the product remains easy to compare with the source.

Turn that product reference into an action scene for a listing or social post. Keep the product visible, compare the result with the captured reference, and add your exact offer in the editor. A clear final pose also gives the editor a useful thumbnail.
